sector_model: Online B2B marketplace and logistics for large-parcel goods: P/E, FCF after reported capex, inventory and receivable turns, lease obligations, tariff sensitivity; working capital swings distort OCF.
thesis: GigaCloud Technology (Nasdaq: GCT), B2B ecommerce marketplace for large-parcel goods (furniture, appliances), Cayman parent with California operations. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read in relevant sections. Q3 revenue 423.6M (+27%), 9M revenue 1,194.7M (+28.9%) vs 927.2M; 9M gross profit 296.7M (24.8% margin vs 23.5%); 9M operating income 149.0M vs 104.7M; 9M NI 131.1M vs 98.9M (+32.6%); effective tax 17.0%. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 374.2M, investments 43.0M, no borrowings, equity 567.9M. 9M OCF 83.1M vs 126.3M (down); capex 8.3M; buybacks 60.0M in 9M. Close 60.44 (2026-11-19) x 35.624M shares = 2.15B = 12.7x TTM NI 169.6M, FCF yield 6.3% (TTM FCF 136.4M), 3.8x book (own arithmetic). Possible market view: a tariff-exposed, consumer-cyclical furniture importer whose growth and margins are peak. Differing evidence: accelerating revenue (+27% in Q3 vs about +25% 9M25 pace not verified), margin expansion, net cash, falling share count (29.64M to 29.26M Class A). Not a recommendation.
counterthesis: Operating cash flow fell 34% in 9M while NI rose 33%: inventory up 16% and receivables up 31% since year end absorbed cash; if demand slows, inventory write-downs follow. Tariffs, ocean freight and U.S. housing demand drive results and were not analysed from the 10-Q risk factors. Dual-class structure (6.46M Class B) concentrates control. 474.7M of operating lease liabilities are fixed obligations on a 718.6M liability base. Selling and marketing up 48% in 9M. Peers and history not compared; the 11-13 officer or director change was not read.
invalidation: Invalidated by sustained revenue decline or gross margin below about 22%, inventory growth continuing to outpace sales, OCF staying below NI for several quarters, tariff changes that cut import economics, or governance problems.
